chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Hamzah ibn Ya'la, from Ubaydillah ibn al-Hasan, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who makes his own self detestable (to himself) rather than making the people detestable (to him), Allah will protect him from the terror of the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.مَقَتَ: To hate, detest, or make detestable

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of making one's own self detestable rather than making people detestable?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual discipline of *muhasabah* (self-accounting), where internalizing one's faults prevents the arrogance of blaming others. This self-criticism serves as a shield against the *Faza'* (great terror) of the Day of Judgment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner purification over external validation. It underscores that true safety comes from aligning one’s self-perception with divine accountability rather than social approval.
